Figure 3 relates chromatin modules to single-cell accessibility and linked-gene expression. Module definitions, native Seurat scoring, link selection and the DotPlot transformation are included directly below. A default render uses saved numerical outputs.

Accessibility scores use the stored interval TF-IDF data; marker and linked-gene expression use SCT. UMAP coordinates and Cell_Type_3 labels are preserved. Dot size measures the fraction of raw module scores above zero, not the fraction of individual peaks detected. The linked-gene heatmap contains module gene-set scores, not individual-gene rows. A16 pools the five source modules specified in the module key.

## Inputs and saved objects

Paths are relative to the `CortexCode/` directory. **saved-results** inputs support routine rendering; **optional-rerun** inputs are read only when the corresponding analysis is enabled. Wildcards identify file collections.

| Mode | Input path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| saved-results | `data/source_tables/Fig3_KC/*.csv` | Fig3_KC: numerical plotting tables (collection) |
| saved-results | `data/source_tables/Extended_Fig5_KC/*.csv` | Extended_Fig5_KC: numerical plotting tables (collection) |
| saved-results | `data/upstream/multiome/atac_modules.csv` | Original interval-to-module assignments; used by panel 5l |
| saved-results | `data/upstream/multiome/Hes1_Tbr1_RNA_cells.csv` | Per-cell Hes1/Tbr1 expression for RNA violins |
| saved-results | `provenance/Extended5l_module_palette.csv` | Native panel 5l module order and colors |
| optional-rerun | `objects/Fig3/exact_V2_cache.rds` | Stored normalized SCT and interval layers, metadata, links and embeddings |

See [input locations](INPUTS.md), [saved R objects](SAVED_OBJECTS.md) and the [complete file inventory](config/file_inventory.csv) for original source names, sizes and availability. These large inputs are not part of the Git checkout.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/common.R")
repo_dir <- REPO
if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) params <- list()
if (is.null(params$run_multiome)) params$run_multiome <- FALSE

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  error = FALSE)
```

## Original module definitions

Weak P2 source modules are pooled; four smaller source modules are included in Constitutive_strong. The A16 label therefore refers to the pooled set in Figure 3. This explicit mapping is specific to the supplied multiome analysis and should not be replaced with a one-to-one lookup from the bulk ATAC catalog.

```{r multiome-original-module-definitions, eval=isTRUE(params$run_multiome)}
checkpoint_dir <- file.path(REPO, "objects", "Fig3")
module_table <- read.csv(
  file.path(repo_dir, "data", "upstream", "multiome", "atac_modules.csv"),
  row.names = 1
)
module_table$Module[module_table$Module %in% c("P2_specific", "RBP_specific")] <- "Weak_P2"
module_table$Module[module_table$Module %in% c("pink", "black", "greenyellow", "lightcyan", "Constitutive_strong")] <- "Constitutive_strong"
module_table$Module[module_table$Module == "Weak_late"] <- "Weak_neuronal"
module_table$Module[module_table$Module == "Weak_middle"] <- "Weak_immature"
```

## Stored assays and native scoring

The original scoring uses 24 bins, 100 control draws per feature and seed 1, reset separately for each module. The data layer is used directly. The dummy assay below only provides a container; no dummy values contribute to any score.

```{r multiome-stored-assays-and-native-scoring, eval=isTRUE(params$run_multiome)}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  {
    library(Matrix)
    library(Seurat)
    library(dplyr)
  }
)
cache <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoint_dir, "exact_V2_cache.rds"))
cells <- rownames(cache$metadata)
dummy_counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
  1,
  nrow = 1,
  ncol = length(cells),

  sparse = TRUE,
  dimnames = list("container", cells)
)
multiome <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = Seurat::CreateAssayObject(counts = dummy_counts),


  assay = "container",
  meta.data = cache$metadata
)
multiome[["intervals"]] <- Seurat::CreateAssayObject(data = cache$intervals)
multiome[["SCT"]] <- Seurat::CreateAssayObject(data = cache$SCT)
peak_sets <- split(module_table$interval, module_table$Module)
for (module in names(peak_sets)) {
  multiome <- Seurat::AddModuleScore(
    object = multiome,
    features = list(peak_sets[[module]]),

    assay = "intervals",
    name = paste0(module, "_ATAC"),

    nbin = 24,
    ctrl = 100,
    seed = 1,
    slot = "data"
  )
}
```

## Linked-gene selection and expression scores

Positive links are defined by zscore >= 0. For each interval, retain the smallest link P value, with the original first-row tie rule (`with_ties = FALSE`). Genes are deduplicated within module; one gene may belong to more than one module. Scores use SCT, not the RNA assay.

```{r multiome-linked-gene-selection-and-expression-scores, eval=isTRUE(params$run_multiome)}
module_links <- module_table[, c("interval", "Module")]
names(module_links) <- c("query_region", "Module")
selected_links <- cache$links %>%
  filter(zscore >= 0) %>%
  left_join(module_links, by = "query_region") %>%
  group_by(query_region) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = pvalue,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
gene_sets <- lapply(
  split(selected_links$linked_gene, selected_links$Module),
  unique
)
for (module in names(gene_sets)) {
  multiome <- Seurat::AddModuleScore(
    object = multiome,
    features = list(gene_sets[[module]]),

    assay = "SCT",
    name = paste0(module, "_RNA"),

    nbin = 24,
    ctrl = 100,
    seed = 1,
    slot = "data"
  )
}
```

## Plot statistics and scaling

For cluster c and raw module score s: dot size is 100 × mean(s > 0). Seurat DotPlot averages expm1(s), then applies log1p and standardization across the 16 clusters, clipping color at ±2.5. Figure 3c clips negative scores to zero for display only. The linked-gene heatmap centers module scores across cells, divides by sample SD, applies the ScaleData upper cap of 10, and clips the displayed colors at ±2.5. The heatmap rows represent module gene-set scores, not individual genes.

```{r multiome-dot-statistics, eval=isTRUE(params$run_multiome)}
dot_statistics <- function(score, cluster) {
  groups <- split(score, cluster)
  average <- vapply(
    groups, function(x) mean(expm1(x)),
    numeric(1)
  )
  percent_positive <- vapply(
    groups, function(x) 100 *
      mean(x > 0),
    numeric(1)
  )
  color <- as.numeric(scale(log1p(average)))

  data.frame(
    Cluster = names(groups),
    Average_expm1_score = average,
    Percent_positive = percent_positive,

    Color = pmax(-2.5, pmin(2.5, color))
  )
}
```


## Native module-score heatmap scaling

Rows of Figure 3d are linked-gene module scores. The original workflow creates a score assay, scales each score across cells and displays the stored cell-type order. This code leaves gene-set membership and SCT normalization unchanged.

```{r native-score-heatmap, eval=isTRUE(params$run_multiome)}
rna_score_columns <- grep(
  "_RNA1$", colnames(multiome[[]]),
  value = TRUE
)
score_matrix <- t(as.matrix(multiome[[]][, rna_score_columns, drop = FALSE]))
multiome[["RNA_module_scores"]] <- Seurat::CreateAssayObject(data = score_matrix)
multiome <- Seurat::ScaleData(
  multiome,
  assay = "RNA_module_scores",
  features = rownames(score_matrix),

  do.center = TRUE,
  do.scale = TRUE,
  scale.max = 10
)
heatmap <- Seurat::DoHeatmap(
  multiome,
  assay = "RNA_module_scores",
  features = rownames(score_matrix),

  group.by = "Cell_Type_3",
  disp.min = -2.5,
  disp.max = 2.5
)
saveRDS(multiome[[]], file.path(checkpoint_dir, "recomputed_module_scores.rds"))
```

## Figure 3b: exact dot-plot scores

The final figure shows A1–A15. Size and color are independently named columns in the source data.

```{r figure-3b-exact-dot-plot-scores-3}
d <- read_table("Fig3_KC", "3b_Dotplot_values")
d$Figure_module <- factor(d$Figure_module, levels = rev(paste0("A", 1:15)))
d$Cluster <- factor(d$Cluster, levels = clusters)
stopifnot(
  nrow(d) == 240, all(d$Percent_score_above_zero >= 0 & d$Percent_score_above_zero <= 100)
)
p <- ggplot(
  d, aes(
    Cluster,
    Figure_module,
    size = Percent_score_above_zero,
    color = Dotplot_scaled_color
  )
) +
  geom_point() + scale_size_area(max_size = 6,
    limits = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",
    limits = c(-2.5, 2.5)
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90,
    vjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    size = "% score > 0",
    color = "Scaled score")
# Category stripe follows the module order; cluster strip uses the UMAP palette.
module_strip <- unique(d["Figure_module"])
module_strip$Position <- as.numeric(module_strip$Figure_module)
module_number <- as.integer(sub("A", "", as.character(module_strip$Figure_module)))
module_strip$Category <- ifelse(module_number <= 3, "Early", ifelse(module_number <= 11, "Intermediate", "Late"))
cluster_strip <- data.frame(Position = seq_along(clusters))
p <- p +
  geom_rect(data = module_strip,
    aes(ymin = Position - 0.5, ymax = Position + 0.5),
    xmin = 0.25, xmax = 0.48, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = unname(MS$category[module_strip$Category]), color = NA) +
  geom_rect(data = cluster_strip,
    aes(xmin = Position - 0.45, xmax = Position + 0.45),
    ymin = 0.15, ymax = 0.40, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = unname(cluster_colors[clusters]), color = NA) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) gsub("_", "", x), expand = expansion(add = c(0.85, 0.6))) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.9, 0.6)))
export_panel(p, "Fig3/3b_dotplot", 3.8, 3.8)
```

## Extended Figure 5l: cluster-enriched accessible intervals

The bar represents the composition of positively enriched accessible intervals within each cluster, rather than all significant increases and decreases. The reconstructed display rule is adjusted P < 0.001, average log2FC > 0.5 and detection in at least 25% of cells in the cluster. The denominator is the number of retained intervals in that cluster. A peak may contribute to more than one cluster, but is counted once within a cluster.

Use Nic's module pooling before counting: pink, black, greenyellow and lightcyan join Constitutive_strong; P2_specific/RBP_specific join Weak_P2; Weak_middle and Weak_late become Weak_immature and Weak_neuronal. The display filters naturally leave 16 pooled groups. No module is discarded merely to match the artwork. The filter/pooling combination reproduces the saved native bar image to approximately two pixels at its original resolution. The exact original plotting statement was not supplied; the inclusive 25% boundary is explicit. Several adjusted-P thresholds yield identical retained rows and cannot be distinguished from this plot alone.

```{r extended5l-positive-accessibility-definition}
plot_extended5l_positive_DA <- function() {
  d <- read_table("Extended_Fig5_KC", "5l_Significant_DA_intervals")
  key <- read.csv(file.path(REPO, "data/upstream/multiome/atac_modules.csv"),
    row.names = 1)
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(key$interval), all(d$interval %in% key$interval))
  d$Source_bulk_module <- d$Module
  d$Source_module <- key$Module[match(d$interval, key$interval)]
  pool <- c(pink = "Constitutive_strong", black = "Constitutive_strong",
    greenyellow = "Constitutive_strong", lightcyan = "Constitutive_strong",
    P2_specific = "Weak_P2", RBP_specific = "Weak_P2",
    Weak_middle = "Weak_immature", Weak_late = "Weak_neuronal")
  selected <- d[d$p_val_adj < 0.001 & d$avg_log2FC > 0.5 & d$pct.1 >= 0.25, ]
  selected$Pooled_module <- selected$Source_module
  change <- selected$Pooled_module %in% names(pool)
  selected$Pooled_module[change] <- pool[selected$Pooled_module[change]]
  palette <- read.csv(file.path(REPO, "provenance/Extended5l_module_palette.csv"))
  stopifnot(setequal(unique(selected$Pooled_module), palette$Source_module),
    !anyDuplicated(paste(selected$cluster, selected$interval)))
  selected$Module <- palette$Module[match(selected$Pooled_module, palette$Source_module)]
  counts <- selected %>% count(cluster, Module, name = "DA_interval_count") %>%
    complete(cluster = clusters, Module = palette$Module,
      fill = list(DA_interval_count = 0)) %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    mutate(Cluster_total = sum(DA_interval_count),
      Proportion = DA_interval_count / Cluster_total) %>% ungroup()
  stopifnot(sum(counts$DA_interval_count) == nrow(selected),
    all(abs(tapply(counts$Proportion, counts$cluster, sum) - 1) < 1e-12))
  counts$cluster <- factor(counts$cluster, levels = clusters)
  counts$Module <- factor(counts$Module, levels = palette$Module)
  p <- ggplot(counts, aes(cluster, Proportion, fill = Module)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.92) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(palette$Color, palette$Module), drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) gsub("_", "", x)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Proportion of DA intervals", fill = "Modules") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_family = "Arial") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9), legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.key.height = grid::unit(3.3, "mm"), legend.key.width = grid::unit(4, "mm"))
  export_panel(p, "Ext5/5l_DA_modules", 6.4, 4.8,
    note = "Positive cluster-enriched intervals: adjusted P<0.001, log2FC>0.5, detection>=25%; native module pooling; within-cluster denominator")
  write.csv(counts, file.path(REPO,
    "data/source_tables/Extended_Fig5_KC/5l_Positive_DA_module_proportions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(counts, file.path(REPO,
    "data/source_tables/Extended_Fig5_KC/5l_DA_module_proportions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  save_object(list(counts = counts, selected_intervals = selected,
    filter = list(adjusted_P = 0.001, log2FC_greater_than = 0.5,
      detection_at_least = 0.25), module_pooling = pool, palette = palette),
    "multiome/5l_positive_DA_composition")
}
```

## Extended Figure 5 PCA from saved VST inputs

Only the inexpensive prcomp projection is rerun as a numerical check; the original DESeq2 transformation is not refitted.

```{r extended-figure-5-pca-from-saved-vst-inputs-7}
for (panel in c("5h", "5j")) {
  d <- read_table("Extended_Fig5_KC", paste0(panel, "_PCA_coordinates"))
  v <- read_table("Extended_Fig5_KC", paste0(panel, "_VST_inputs"))
  pc <- prcomp(
    t(numeric_matrix(v)),
    center = TRUE,
    scale. = FALSE
  )
  stopifnot(
    max(
      abs(
        abs(pc$x[, 1]) -
          abs(d$PC1)
      )
    ) <
      1e-07
  )
  d$PCA_class <- sub("_.*", "", d$Cluster)
  d$Label <- gsub("_", "-", d$Cluster)
  variance <- summary(pc)$importance[2, 1:2]
  p <- ggplot(d,
    aes(Plot_PC1, Plot_PC2, color = PCA_class, label = Label)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_text(vjust = -0.6,
      size = 2.4) +
    scale_color_manual(values = MS$pca_class) +
    labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.0f%% variance)", 100 * variance[1]),
      y = sprintf("PC2 (%.0f%% variance)", 100 * variance[2]), color = "Class")
  export_panel(
    p, paste0("Ext5/", panel, "_PCA"),
    6, 5
  )
  save_object(pc, paste0("multiome/", panel, "_PCA"))
}
plot_extended5l_positive_DA()
```

## Gene-expression insets

These use the saved normalized RNA data layer, not the SCT values used for marker overlays. Fine clusters are collapsed to RG, IPC and CPN without changing expression values.

```{r figure-3-rna-insets}
rna <- read.csv(file.path(REPO, "data/upstream/multiome/Hes1_Tbr1_RNA_cells.csv"))
stopifnot(nrow(rna) == 13625, !anyDuplicated(rna$Cell_ID),
  all(is.finite(rna$Hes1)), all(is.finite(rna$Tbr1)),
  setequal(rna$Cell_ID, read_table("Fig3_KC", "3d_Heatmap_values")$Cell_ID))
rna$Population <- factor(sub("_.*", "", rna$Cell_Type_3), levels = c("CPN", "IPC", "RG"))
for (gene in c("Hes1", "Tbr1")) {
  p <- ggplot(rna, aes(.data[[gene]], Population, fill = Population)) +
    geom_violin(orientation = "y", scale = "width", linewidth = 0.35) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(RG = "#F8766D", IPC = "#00BA38", CPN = "#619CFF")) +
    scale_y_discrete(position = "right") +
    labs(title = paste(gene, "RNA"), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold.italic"))
  key <- data.frame(Category = factor(c("Early", "Intermediate", "Late", "Constitutive"),
    levels = c("Constitutive", "Late", "Intermediate", "Early")), x = 0)
  legend <- ggplot(key, aes(x, Category, fill = Category)) +
    geom_point(shape = 22, size = 3, color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = Category), x = 0.12, hjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = MS$category) + xlim(-0.1, 1) +
    labs(title = "WGCNA module\ncategory") + theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))
  inset <- p / legend + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1.5, 1))
  export_panel(inset, paste0("Fig3/3ef_", gene, "_RNA"), 1.8, 2.7)
}
```
